$comment: High-intent query detection for `npm run insights` (scripts/lib/intent.mjs). A Search Console query is HIGH-INTENT when it reads like a buyer choosing, not a reader learning: it carries one of the `signals` (software, system, tool, pricing, vs, …) or sits on the `watch` list. Navigational brand queries are excluded by `navigational`. These rows are printed FIRST in every insights pull and worked first in every cadence run (content-cadence step 2) — on a zero-click site they sit far below the informational rows by volume, and a run that reads the report top-down never reaches them. `claimFrom` names the collections whose entries declare `primaryKeyword`/`secondaryKeywords` in frontmatter (the money pages): the report cross-checks the page Google shows a query on against the page that claims it and flags `wrong-page` / `unmapped`. `watch` is curated by a human or the weekly keyword-map refresh — the transactional phrasings the site means to win, each tied to the page that claims it, so a zero-impression term is reported as 'not showing yet' instead of silently absent.
$navigationalComment: TODO — your own brand name and its common misspellings, plus other products' names that land on your pages by accident (a query that is somebody else's brand is noise, not a buyer). Filled by /onboard-marketing or by hand; the weekly cadence run adds what the snapshots turn up.
$claimFromComment: TODO — the collections whose entries carry `primaryKeyword` (+ `secondaryKeywords`) frontmatter, with the route each is served under. Example: [{ "collection": "solution", "route": "/solutions" }]. Empty = every high-intent row reads `unmapped` until a page claims it (or the watch list names one).
$watchComment: TODO — one object per transactional phrasing the site means to win: { "query": "<exact words a buyer types>", "page": "/<route that claims it>", "since": "YYYY-MM-DD", "note": "<why it is here, what was done>" }. Add a term the day it first earns an impression (or the day a competitor sweep shows a rival owns it); never retire one — a term that stopped showing is a finding, not noise. Keep `page` in step with that page's frontmatter keywords and with marketing/keyword-map.md § High-intent, in the same commit.
